findings.passage: The legislation increases penalties associated with voter fraud. It orders that whoever knowingly provides false information in connection with automatic voter registration shall be punished by a fine of not more than $10,000 or imprisonment for up to 5 years or both.
findings.note: Press release on her site about the Senate vote on H.4671 (automatic voter registration with anti-fraud penalties). Statement issued on her site; the quoted line is the release's description of the bill, not a personal quote.

findings.passage: We should be making it easier for people to exercise their right to vote, not harder.
findings.note: Her quoted statement on the automatic voter registration bill, about registration access.
Her press release says she joined Senate colleagues in voting to pass H.4671, An Act automatically registering eligible voters and enhancing safeguards against fraud.

findings.passage: The bill would require the Secretary of the Commonwealth to enter into an agreement with ERIC no later than July 1, 2022, which thirty other states have already joined, helping states keep more accurate voting rolls.
findings.note: Press release on her site about Senate passage of S.2545 (VOTES Act). Describes the voter-roll accuracy provision.
Her release says she joined colleagues to pass S.2545, the VOTES Act (permanent mail-in and early voting, same-day registration, ERIC). No ID requirement is described.

findings.passage: Allows election officials to pre-process mail-in and early voting ballots (by opening up envelopes and verifying signatures in advance of Election Day).
findings.note: Press release on her site about the final VOTES Act (S.2924). Mail ballots are checked by signature; the release lists no photo ID requirement.
Her release says she joined colleagues to pass S.2924, the VOTES Act conference agreement. It also requires the state to join ERIC to keep voter rolls accurate.
